findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/SimpleModule/Basic.lean:519-520 `noncomputable instance _root_.Module.End.instDivisionRing [DecidableEq (Module.End R M)] [IsSimpleModule R M] : DivisionRing (Module.End R M)` — the `letI` at Presentation.lean:241 exists solely to discharge that `DecidableEq`, not to make any defeq work. Mathlib keeps this behind an existential (`Mathlib/RingTheory/SimpleModule/WedderburnArtin.lean:196 `classical exact ⟨n, _, d, inferInstance, …⟩`), where the choice cannot leak; here it is an exposed structure field.
findings.fix: Split the comment: keep the defeq sentence adjacent to `equiv := P.equiv`, and add a separate line above the `letI` stating that `Module.End.instDivisionRing` requires `DecidableEq` and that the arbitrary `Classical.decEq` choice becomes part of the exposed `instDivisionRing` field, so downstream results must use `P.toWedderburnAlgebraPresentation.instDivisionRing` rather than re-synthesizing. Mention it in the module docstring's choice paragraph (lines 22-24) alongside block order.
findings.issue: The comment at 238-240 explains why `equiv := P.equiv` typechecks (ring structures agreeing up to unfolding), but it sits directly above the `letI : ∀ i, DecidableEq (Module.End A (P.simpleIdeal i)) := fun _ ↦ Classical.decEq _` at 241, which does something else entirely: it supplies the `DecidableEq` argument of `Module.End.instDivisionRing`. Because `toWedderburnAlgebraPresentation` is `@[expose]`, `Classical.decEq` is frozen into the resulting `instDivisionRing` field, and `toWedderburnAlgebraPresentation_divisionRing` (254-257) exposes only the type, not the instance. A downstream user who re-synthesizes `DivisionRing (Module.End A (P.simpleIdeal i))ᵐᵒᵖ` under a `classical` block gets an instance that is propositionally but not definitionally equal to the field, and nothing in the file warns of this.

summary: Proofs are now short, robust, and free of change/show or brittle rewrite chains; the prior structural findings are addressed. One remaining issue: the comment at the endomorphism-form coercion documents a defeq that is not what the adjacent letI does, leaving the Classical.decEq baked into an @[expose]d instance field undocumented.
